_meta.indication: Victoza is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week double-blind, randomized, controlled trial with an active comparator (glimepiride).
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with diet and exercise (monotherapy), mean baseline HbA1c 8.2%.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in HbA1c after 52 weeks.
pivotal_trials.n: 746 patients randomized to Victoza 1.2 mg (ITT 251), Victoza 1.8 mg (ITT 246), or glimepiride 8 mg (ITT 248).
pivotal_trials.result: Adjusted mean HbA1c change from baseline -1.1% (Victoza 1.8 mg) and -0.8% (Victoza 1.2 mg) vs -0.5% (glimepiride); difference from glimepiride -0.6% (95% CI -0.8, -0.4; p<0.0001) for 1.8 mg and -0.3% (95% CI -0.5, -0.1; p=0.001) for 1.2 mg.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5% and more common than placebo): headache, nausea, diarrhea, and anti-liraglutide antibody formation. In the 52-week monotherapy trial nausea occurred in 28.4% of Victoza vs 8.5% glimepiride, and diarrhea 17.1% vs 8.9%. Serious concerns include pancreatitis and serious hypoglycemia (when used with an insulin secretagogue).
target_moa: Liraglutide is an acylated human GLP-1 receptor agonist with 97% amino acid sequence homology to endogenous human GLP-1(7-37); like GLP-1(7-37) it activates the GLP-1 receptor, enhancing glucose-dependent insulin secretion.
modality: peptide (acylated human GLP-1 analog produced by recombinant DNA)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF THYROID C-CELL TUMORS. Liraglutide causes dose-dependent and treatment-duration-dependent thyroid C-cell tumors at clinically relevant exposures in both genders of rats and mice; human relevance is unknown. Victoza is contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of MTC or Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).

rems.type: A REMS was approved consisting of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.

advisory_committee.vote: Presented to the Endocrinology and Metabolism Advisory Committee (EMDAC) on April 2, 2009. On cardiovascular safety 8 Yes / 5 No; on whether thyroid C-cell data permit marketing 6 Yes / 6 No / 1 Abstain; on whether animal thyroid findings are not relevant to humans 1 Yes / 12 No; on whether papillary thyroid cancer data permit marketing 12 Yes / 0 No / 1 Abstain.

description.text: Added indication to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and established cardiovascular disease

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application proposes the addition of an indication to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and established cardiovascular disease, and revised labeling to reflect the results of the "Liraglutide Effect and Action in Diabetes: Evaluation of cardiovascular outcome Results" (LEADER) trial.

description.text: Expanded approved age range for type 2 diabetes mellitus to patients 10 years and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for updates to the Victoza labeling to expand the approved age range of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus to 10 years and older to reflect the results of the, "Efficacy and safety of liraglutide in combination with metformin versus metformin monotherapy on glycaemic control in children and adolescents with type 2 diabetes - A 26-week double-blind, randomised, parallel group, placebo controlled multi-centre trial followed by a 26-week open-label extension," to fulfill the requirements of a Written Request issued by FDA to Novo Nordisk Inc. dated September 19, 2012, amended January 15, 2015, and March 20, 2017.

summary.text: Victoza (liraglutide) was approved under a traditional (full) approval as a 505(b) new drug application for glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus, based on a 52-week monotherapy trial and four 26-week add-on combination trials; approval was accompanied by a REMS (Medication Guide and communication plan) and numerous required postmarketing studies addressing thyroid C-cell tumor, pancreatitis, and cardiovascular risks. The application was reviewed by the Endocrinology and Metabolism Advisory Committee.

citations.quote: Please refer to your March 23, 2008, new drug application (NDA) submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Victoza (liraglutide [rDNA origin]) injection, solution for subcutaneous use.
The safety of Victoza was evaluated in a 52-week monotherapy trial and in four 26-week, add-on combination therapy trials.

Your proposed REMS, submitted on January 21, 2010, and appended to this letter, is approved. The REMS consists of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.
This NDA was presented before the Endocrinology and Metabolism Advisory Committee (EMDAC) on April 2, 2009.
